teaching.causalExplanation: In a piece of metal, each atom gives up its outer electrons, which are called valence electrons. They don't go to another atom. They spread out through the whole piece of metal, so they're delocalised, meaning they aren't tied to any one atom. What's left behind are positive ions, called cations, packed in a regular lattice. So a metal is a lattice of cations in a sea of moving electrons. The metallic bond is the attraction between the positive cations and the negative electron sea. Here's the key feature. In a covalent bond, the shared electrons sit between two particular atoms, so the bond points in one direction. In a metal, every cation is attracted to the electrons all around it, in every direction. The metallic bond has no fixed direction. Chemists call it non-directional, and that's what lets a metal bend. First, conductivity. A current is a flow of charge, so a conductor needs charged particles that can move. Connect a battery, and the delocalised electrons drift toward the positive terminal, while new electrons flow in from the negative end. The cations stay where they are. They only vibrate. So metals conduct as solids, because their electrons are already free to move. In the salt crystal, the ions are locked in place until it melts or dissolves.

(a) Melting points (PubChem, CRC values): sodium 97.8 °C (shown 98); magnesium 650 °C (sources give 649 to 651); copper 1084.6 °C (not shown); aluminium 660 °C (not shown).
(b) Coin composition: Royal Australian Mint specification for the $1 and $2 coins, aluminium bronze, 92% copper, 6% aluminium, 2% nickel (as v01, root decision 4; science check to confirm).

scenes.teachingReason: Here's a pattern exam questions love. To conduct, a substance needs charged particles that are free to move. In a metal, those are the delocalised electrons, so it conducts as a solid and as a liquid. In an ionic compound, they're the ions, so it conducts only when molten or dissolved. And in a molecular substance, like sugar or pure water, the outer electrons are held in bonds and lone pairs, so there's almost nothing free to carry the charge.

scenes.teachingReason: Now mix in other atoms. An alloy is a metal mixed with other elements.
